exp: 'Although' = contrast (poor but happy).

opts: She requested me to help her.
She said me to help her.
exp: Request in reported speech → 'requested + object + to + verb'.

q: He said to me, 'Open the door.'
opts: He told me to open the door.
He asked me open the door.
exp: Command in reported speech → 'told + object + to + verb'.

opts: She told me to not shout.
She asked me not to shout.
exp: Negative command → 'asked me not to + verb'.
'A number of' → plural verb 'are'.
'The number' → singular verb 'is'.
When 'class' is treated as a unit → singular verb 'is'.
'Neither' = singular subject → 'is'.
'Either…or' → verb agrees with nearer subject (Suresh = singular).
Verb agrees with 'I' (nearest subject) → 'am'.
'Scissors' = always plural noun → 'are'.
'Trousers' = plural noun (pair items) → 'are'.
'News' = uncountable → singular verb 'is'.
Habitual past action → 'used to'.
'Used to' + gerund for familiarity/habit.
'Be + used to + V-ing' = accustomed to.
'Never' at beginning → inversion → 'have I' (Never have I seen).

q: Hardly had he left _____ it started raining.
exp: 'Hardly...when' is the correct pair (not 'than').

q: Not only _____ she smart, but also kind.
exp: Inversion after 'Not only' → 'Not only is she'.

q: He plays well and so _____ I.
exp: 'So do I' = agreement (same tense as main verb 'plays').

q: She sings well, and so _____ her sister.
exp: 'She sings' → 'so does her sister' (third person singular).

q: He doesn't like sweets. Neither _____ I.
exp: 'Neither do I' → correct ellipsis for negative agreement.

q: It was John who _____ the window.
exp: Cleft sentence — 'it was John who broke' (past tense).

q: It is tea that I _____ in the morning.
exp: Present habit → simple present 'drink'.

q: It was in 1947 that India _____ independence.
exp: 'It was' + past clause → simple past 'got'.

q: He is so tall _____ he touches the fan.
exp: 'So…that' → result clause.

q: It was such a hot day _____ we stayed home.
exp: 'Such…that' → result clause.

q: The movie was so boring _____ I left early.
exp: 'So…that' structure showing result.
'Had better' is a strong suggestion/warning.
'Would rather' → preference (I prefer to die than beg).
Correct idiom: 'would rather + verb'.
Emphatic pronoun 'myself' — past tense 'baked'.
Past tense with emphatic 'himself'.
'Themselves' → plural → 'cleaned' (past tense).
Zero conditional: If + present, present → melts (universal truth).

q: If I were rich, I _____ a car.
exp: Second conditional: Imaginary → 'would buy'.

q: If I had known, I _____ helped.
exp: Third conditional: Past regret → 'would have' + V3.
'Too + adj + to + verb' — 'to' is the connector.

q: He is strong enough _____ lift it.
exp: 'Enough + to + verb' — 'to' follows 'enough'.

q: The bag is too heavy _____ carry.
exp: 'Too…to' structure — 'to carry'.
Let + object + base verb (no 'to').
'Make' + object + base verb (causative).
'Help' can be followed by base verb or 'to' + verb (both correct).
Adjective order: Size → Colour → Noun (small red ball).

q: A beautiful old French house — is this correct?
exp: Opinion → Age → Origin → Noun — correct order.
Correct order: Size → Colour → Material (big black leather).

q: My brother he is smart. — Is this correct?
exp: Remove 'he' — 'My brother' is already the subject (redundant pronoun).

q: The reason is because he was late. — Is this correct?
exp: 'The reason is that…' is correct — not 'the reason is because'.

q: The patient he recovered fast. — Is this correct?
exp: Redundant pronoun — remove 'he'. 'The patient recovered fast.'

q: I like this shirt, but I prefer that _____.
exp: 'One' for singular noun replacement (shirt).

q: These shoes are better than those _____.
exp: 'Ones' for plural noun replacement (shoes).

q: I'll take the blue ones, not the red _____.
exp: 'Ones' → plural reference (blue ones, red ones).
Always + present simple (she = third person singular → comes).
'Already' comes before past participle in present perfect.

q: Hardly _____ he reached when it rained.
exp: 'Hardly had' = correct past perfect with inversion.
'Much' with uncountable noun (money).
'Many' for countable nouns (friends).
'A lot of + noun' — correct structure.

q: It was so hot _____ I fainted.
exp: 'So…that' construction showing result.

q: She is such a good singer _____ she won.
exp: 'Such…that' structure.

q: It was such an easy paper _____ all passed.
exp: Result clause — 'such an easy paper that all passed'.

q: Neither the girl nor the boys _____ happy.
exp: Verb agrees with 'boys' (nearest subject, plural) → 'are'.
Treated as one unit/proverb → singular verb 'waits'.
Plural sense (members have different opinions) → 'are'.
Subject names ending in -s → singular verb 'is'.
Country names treated as singular units → 'is'.
Weight/measurement as a unit → singular 'is'.
'A dozen eggs' — eggs are countable/plural → 'are'.
'Every…and every…' → singular verb 'is'.

q: Neither Rahul nor his brothers _____ here.
exp: Verb agrees with nearer subject 'brothers' (plural) → 'are'.

q: She don't go to college. — Is this correct?
exp: Use 'doesn't' with she/he/it → She doesn't go.

q: He is senior than me. — Is this correct?
exp: Words like senior, junior, inferior, superior take 'to', not 'than' → senior to me.

q: One of the boy is missing. — Is this correct?
exp: 'One of the' is followed by a plural noun → 'boys'.

q: Neither of the answers are correct. — Is this correct?
exp: 'Neither' is singular, so use 'is', not 'are'.

q: The jury were divided in its opinion. — Is this correct?
exp: 'Jury' is plural in this context (divided opinions) → 'their opinion'.

q: He is good in mathematics. — Is this correct?
exp: Use 'good at', not 'good in'.

q: The news are shocking. — Is this correct?
exp: 'News' is uncountable → singular → 'is' shocking.

q: The sceneries here is beautiful. — Is this correct?
exp: 'Scenery' is uncountable → use 'is beautiful', no plural form.

q: Ten miles are a long distance to walk. — Is this correct?
exp: Distance = unit → singular → 'is a long distance'.

q: He as well as his friends have arrived. — Is this correct?
exp: With 'as well as', verb agrees with first subject → 'has arrived'.

q: Neither she nor I is guilty. — Is this correct?
exp: Verb agrees with 'I' (nearest) → 'am guilty'.

q: Each of the boys are ready. — Is this correct?
exp: 'Each' is singular → use 'is ready'.

q: Five years are a long time to wait. — Is this correct?
exp: Time duration = singular unit → 'is' a long time.

q: The quality of the apples are good. — Is this correct?
exp: Subject = quality (singular) → 'is good'.

q: The number of students are increasing. — Is this correct?
exp: 'The number' is singular → use 'is increasing'.

q: The police is investigating the matter. — Is this correct?
exp: 'Police' = always plural noun → 'are investigating'.

q: She is one of the girls who has topped the exam. — Is this correct?
exp: 'Who' refers to 'girls' (plural) → 'have topped'.

q: Each boy and each girl are ready. — Is this correct?
exp: Repetition of 'each' → singular verb → 'is ready'.
